classification: pre-registered MC-advantage parameter confirmation and regime-conditioning falsification on the R385 stable platform; research-only
question: Can the R385 stable platform be improved by selecting a practically rounded five-parameter portfolio configuration from the 96 actual R385 Monte Carlo backtests using only the first three one-year training folds, and does any economically motivated market-state switch improve that fixed configuration on the 2025-05-06 holdout?

disclosure.scope: The R385 96 parameter outcomes, a small set of regime-switch mappings and local parameter ranges were inspected before R386 registration.
disclosure.status: R386 is a disclosed confirmation test, not a blind discovery.
disclosure.protection: The MC-advantage candidate and defensive comparator are selected exclusively from the first three 252-return training folds. The 2025-05-06 holdout is evaluated only after those choices are fixed.
disclosure.reason: The user requested continued actual-backtest optimization, so the already observed information is disclosed rather than presented as an independent discovery.

base.purpose: Incremental comparator; it is not re-estimated in R386.

monte_carlo_parameter_synthesis.advantage_selection: Among eligible rounded candidates, maximize mean annualised return over the three training folds; tie-break by worst fold annual return, then median fold Sharpe, then lower c_satellite_cap.
monte_carlo_parameter_synthesis.defensive_selection: Among eligible rounded candidates, maximize worst fold annual return; tie-break by median fold Sharpe, then lower mean equity exposure proxy.
monte_carlo_parameter_synthesis.regime_comparator: The selected advantage candidate is the fixed default. The defensive candidate is used only as the off-state leg of the predeclared regime mappings.

regime_mappings.mechanism: At a month-end, use the latest already-observed regime row to select the next month's complete portfolio curve. Any switch pays 0.52% of changed notional at the rebalance. No leverage is permitted.

rules.state_strength: advantage if lagged state is strong or lean_strong; otherwise defensive
rules.state_nonweak: advantage if lagged state is strong, lean_strong or range; otherwise defensive
rules.trend_breadth: advantage if lagged trend_score >= 50 and above_ma20_pct >= 0.50; otherwise defensive
rules.score_trend: advantage if lagged 20-day mean score >= 55 and lagged trend_score >= 50; otherwise defensive
rules.vol_trend: advantage if lagged 20-day index volatility <= its lagged trailing 252-day median and lagged trend_score >= 50; otherwise defensive

regime_mappings.selection: At most one mapping may advance. If several advance, choose highest worst-fold annual, then highest mean-fold annual, then fewer switches.
regime_mappings.rejection_rule: If no mapping clears the training rule gate and the holdout incremental gate, regime conditioning is negative knowledge and the fixed advantage parameter remains the candidate.

local_monte_carlo.method: Latin hypercube around the selected advantage candidate, followed by the same practical rounding

five_x.role: diagnostic warning only; never a hard rejection

no_leverage.applies_to: candidate, all axis neighbours, all local Monte Carlo samples and 5x diagnostic

stable_platform_rationale.claim: A stable platform is chosen because eligibility is broad and perturbation-resistant, not because one cell has the highest realised return. The highest-return cell may be reported for transparency but cannot replace the pre-registered centre after observing results.
required_evidence: 11/11 local axis neighbours pass both costs
at least 95% of local Monte Carlo draws pass both costs
fixed centre is not dominated across the R385 rolling selector comparison

decision_rules: Verify all source hashes and the R385 candidate status before reading R386 performance.
Select the MC-advantage and defensive parameters using training folds only.
Apply the holdout gate to the already selected fixed advantage parameter and the already selected defensive comparator.
A regime mapping advances only if it clears its training rule gate and all candidate incremental and holdout gates; it must also beat the fixed advantage parameter on holdout return and Sharpe.
Regime rejection does not reject a passing fixed advantage parameter; it records negative knowledge for market-state switching.
All local axis neighbours and at least 95% of unique local Monte Carlo draws must pass both 2x and 3x gates.
No threshold may be changed after R386 performance is read.
5x remains warning-only and never rejects a no-leverage passing candidate.
A complete pass may set status candidate_for_paper_trading_review only; no paper targets, orders or production configuration are generated.
known_limits: The holdout and several regime mappings were observed in scratch analysis before registration; R386 is a disclosed confirmation test, not a blind out-of-sample study.
The underlying stock-selection backtests remain daily T+1 approximations and do not model intraday market impact.
regime_history state changes almost daily and its latest row ends before the R385 backtest end; month-end selection carries the latest known state.
The 96 R385 parameter draws and the 124 unique local draws are correlated, not independent multiple-testing trials.
Parameter synthesis perturbs portfolio construction only; A, B and C stock selection remain fixed.
Historical industry classification is not a complete publication-vintage history.
No leverage is evaluated or permitted.
